nodes.content: Develop tactile slip prediction that distinguishes impending grasp slip from elastic deformation across unseen materials and sensor wear.
requirements: Predict slip at least 100 milliseconds ahead with ≥90% recall and ≤5% false-positive rate.
Meet targets on held-out materials and worn sensors, including deformation-only contacts matched for force.

nodes.content: Train a force-conditioned tactile model using shear-drift and strain-recovery signals, matched-force deformation negatives, and wear augmentation for 120-ms slip forecasts.
Can force-conditioned shear-drift and strain-recovery cues distinguish incipient slip from force-matched elastic deformation on worn sensors?
Force-conditioned cues achieve ≥90% 120-ms slip recall at ≤5% false-positive rate on worn, unseen materials and force-matched deformation.
Collect force-matched slip/deformation trials; train a wear-augmented cue model; calibrate and test 120-ms forecasts on held-out materials and worn sensors.
Run WearSlip-120 leave-material-and-wear-out testing, measuring 120-ms slip recall and false-positive rate on force-matched deformation-only contacts.
WearSlip-120 held-out-material, worn-sensor tests achieved 92% 120-ms slip recall and 3.8% false-positive rate on force-matched deformation-only contacts.
Adopt force-conditioned cue model for deployment testing: WearSlip-120 meets recall and deformation false-positive thresholds on held-out materials and worn sensors.
After adoption, test closed-loop gripper interventions on unseen materials and worn sensors, measuring drop rate and deformation-triggered false interventions.
Run GripLoop-120 closed-loop trials on unseen materials with worn sensors, logging drops and force-matched deformation-triggered grip adjustments.
GripLoop-120 archive contains worn-sensor tactile traces on unseen materials, intervention timestamps, drop labels, and force-matched deformation-triggered adjustment annotations.
Audit GripLoop-120 timestamp alignment and annotation completeness; calculate drop rate and deformation-triggered intervention rate from validated trials.
Audited GripLoop-120 held-out-material, worn-sensor trials cut drops from 8.4% to 2.1%, with 3.6% deformation-triggered interventions.
At 90% 120-ms slip recall, strain-recovery cues halve deformation false alarms versus shear-drift-only models on worn sensors.
Measure deformation false-positive rates for full versus shear-drift-only models at 90% 120-ms recall on WearSlip-120 held-out materials and worn sensors.
On WearSlip-120 at 90% 120-ms recall, deformation false-positive rates were 3.3% versus 4.5% for shear-only, not halved.
Can per-contact normalization control abrasion-induced taxel gain drift without suppressing 120-ms slip precursors?
Ablate per-contact taxel normalization across WearSlip-120 wear levels; compare 120-ms recall and deformation false-positive rate against unnormalized input.
WearSlip-120 normalization ablation report contains wear-stratified 120-ms recall and deformation false-positive rates against unnormalized baselines.
Forecast 120-ms slip from peripheral microslip-front propagation versus reversible strain, using per-session marker calibration to tolerate sensor wear.
Do peripheral microslip fronts precede grasp slip without appearing in force-matched elastic deformation, even after marker calibration on worn sensors?
Peripheral-front propagation predicts slip ≥120 ms ahead with ≥90% recall and ≤5% deformation false positives on worn sensors.
Using the normalization ablation report, measure calibrated microslip-front 120-ms recall and force-matched deformation false positives on worn, held-out WearSlip-120 contacts.
WearSlip-120 calibrated fronts reached 91% 120-ms recall but 11% false positives on force-matched deformation-only worn-sensor contacts.
Gating calibrated microslip fronts by short-window strain recovery reduces worn-sensor deformation false positives to ≤5% at ≥90% 120-ms recall.
Using the normalization-ablation report, compare strain-recovery-gated and ungated fronts' 120-ms recall and force-matched deformation false-positive rates on worn WearSlip-120 sensors.
On worn, held-out WearSlip-120 contacts, recovery gating retained 90.5% 120-ms recall while reducing deformation false positives from 11% to 4.4%.
Retain the force-conditioned model as deployment baseline; advance recovery-gated fronts to comparison, given GripLoop drop reductions and WearSlip threshold compliance.
Benchmark recovery-gated fronts against the retained baseline on worn, held-out WearSlip-120 trials, measuring 120-ms recall and force-matched deformation false-positive rates.
Score both frozen models on identical WearSlip-120 held-out-material, worn-sensor splits; tabulate 120-ms recall and deformation false-positive rates.
WearSlip-120 paired-model scorecard lists frozen-model 120-ms recall and deformation false-positive rates by held-out material and sensor-wear level.
Audit WearSlip-120 scorecard splits and GripLoop-120 timestamps/labels; recompute per-wear recall, deformation false positives, drop and false-intervention rates.
Audited worst-wear held-out silicone: baseline achieved 85% 120-ms recall and 7% deformation false positives; gated fronts achieved 91% and 4.2%.
Replicate audited worst-wear silicone results across three sensor batches, comparing both models’ 120-ms recall and force-matched deformation false-positive rates.
Across three worst-wear silicone batches, gated fronts achieved 91–93% 120-ms recall and 3.8–4.6% deformation false positives; baseline missed thresholds.
Does per-session marker calibration remain valid through progressive abrasion, or does front-timing drift erode the 120-ms warning?
Using three-batch benchmarks and the WearSlip-120 scorecard, measure recalibrated front-timing drift, 120-ms recall, and deformation false positives through abrasion.
After 4,000 within-session abrasion cycles, calibrated fronts drifted 28 ms; held-out silicone 120-ms recall fell to 84%.
Defer deployment; pursue online recalibration for gated fronts because abrasion breaks recall, while the baseline already fails worst-wear thresholds.
Update marker calibration during stable-contact intervals when marker residual exceeds 2 pixels, retaining recovery-gated 120-ms slip forecasts.
Can stable-contact recalibration correct abrasion-induced front-timing drift without absorbing elastic deformation into the marker baseline?
Online stable-contact recalibration restores ≥90% 120-ms recall and ≤5% force-matched deformation false positives after 4,000 abrasion cycles.
Implement deformation-screened stable-contact recalibration; test 120-ms recall and force-matched deformation false positives after 4,000 abrasion cycles.
Select taxel normalization from WearSlip-120 ablation; implement stable-contact, deformation-screened marker updates triggered by >2-pixel residuals during abrasion trials.
WearCal-v1 implements normalized, deformation-screened marker updates at >2-pixel residuals and logs update timing during abrasion trials.
Audit WearCal-v1 updates and compare 4,000-cycle drift, 120-ms recall, and force-matched deformation false positives against frozen calibration on held-out silicone.
After 4,000 cycles, WearCal-v1 cut drift to 7 ms; held-out silicone reached 92% 120-ms recall, 4.3% force-matched deformation false positives.
Does slow creep during 30-second holds pass WearCal-v1’s stable-contact screen and increase deformation false positives?
Challenge WearCal-v1 with 30-second force-matched creep holds after abrasion; audit update acceptance, deformation false positives, and 120-ms recall.
In 30-second abrasion-aged creep holds, WearCal-v1 accepted 1.2% of deformation updates; false positives remained 4.7% at 91% 120-ms recall.
Resume closed-loop testing with WearCal-v1, not deployment: abrasion and creep pass thresholds, but prior GripLoop gains predate recalibration.
